player 0: Thanks for specifying exact tiles. I will evaluate if accepting your contract strictly benefits me.

**If I accept:**
- I pay 2 R chips for you at (1,0) and (3,2).
- You promise to cover up to six of my B tile entries (on the tiles you specified).
- My original path to the goal needs no B chips from you—my optimal route is almost entirely R and G.
- But, by using the B-heavy path and letting you pay, I can keep more of my own chips, scoring more at the end.

**Let me calculate chip retention if I take the full B route with your offer:**
My inventory: {'B': 0, 'G': 2, 'R': 14}

Alternate path, B-heavy, positions:
- (0,0) → (0,1) [R] → (0,2) [R] → (0,3) [B] → (1,3) [R] → (2,3) [B] → (3,3) [G]

But on this B-heavy path, B tiles are at (0,3) and (2,3), which you did **not** promise to cover.
Your B coverage is for: (0,3), (1,1), (2,0), (2,1), (3,0), (3,1)  
If I reroute onto those tiles, it is longer and less efficient. I do not need those unless I want to walk a very long path.

**Selfish reasoning:** My optimal path costs me only R and G; adding a detour to use your B chips on those other tiles would force a longer, chip-wasting walk.

**Strictly selfish conclusion:** Your offer doesn't make me strictly better off—I already reach the goal at max efficiency without needing any B chips, and adding a detour to use the B chips you cover would cost me more than it saves.

**Counter-proposal:** If you want my R chips at (1,0) and (3,2), I require that you at minimum cover my B on (0,3) and (2,3) so that my score increases (as I can retain more Rs at the end).

**Counter-offer:**
- (1,0): I give you an R
- (3,2): I give you an R
- (0,3): You give me a B
- (2,3): You give me a B

If you accept, I benefit by saving 2 Rs and spending 2 of your Bs, increasing my final chip tally by 2 chips—strictly better for me.

Any other proposal does not strictly benefit me, so I will not accept.

Let me know if you agree.
